mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months signals an easing monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with FEDFUNDS declining for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate falling below 4.0% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances with UNRATE below 4.0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand expansion, which together predict positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint positive movement of HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100) combined with sub-1.5% annualized GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates economic contraction risk, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods meeting the recession risk regime condition.

mechanism_narrative: Rising quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) signals expanding economic activity that supports corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth rate fails to predict positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of periods.

mechanism_narrative: Annualized CPI inflation exceeding 2.5% signals persistent inflation that may trigger monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL annualized inflation exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous employment growth (PAYEMS) and unemployment decline (UNRATE) indicate a strengthening labor market that together predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint positive PAYEMS and negative UNRATE movement fails to predict positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate above 2.0% during a monetary tightening regime signals higher borrowing costs that depress equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.0%.
